boxes.comments: Complete opening phrase. Q has a broad loop and crossing lower stroke, followed by two low bodies read ue. In donneraient, d has a low oval and taller loop; the following o and repeated n bodies are compressed and flat, followed by low e/r, a rounded a, a detached i dot, and a final rising angular t. No punctuation is visible in the box.

The central applique has a very low initial a, two long downward p strokes, a tall narrow l loop, an i dot, and q with a long descender followed by low u/e. The following à has a small body and detached upper accent. The next neighboring word reaches the right boundary and is not completed in the TSV. A clipped upper-edge curve belongs to the preceding line.

Read remplacé: small initial r-like cup, compressed low e/m run, long descending p, high l loop, low a/c bodies, and final e with detached acute. The p descender and l ascender form a large joined loop arrangement. No additional word or punctuation is supplied.

The prefix relati has initial r/e, tall l loop, low a, crossed t, and dotted i. The final open cup and flattened right ending favor ve, while on remains a graphical alternative. The doubt is localized to these two letters. A separate terminal point is retained. A smaller lower point after the first connected group is not securely established as a punctuation token.
Complete hom abbreviation: tall plain h stem and low shoulder, followed by a low flattened o/m run ending in a short downward hook. No separate full stop is visible. The abbreviation is not expanded.

Complete vertical diagram and label. The source label is (4), with an open upper angle, crosswise segment, and descending right stem. Both E forms have two curved lobes and are rendered calligraphic to record their visible form. The upper E has a smaller open-entry U with a further lowered S; the lower E has S. The connector runs downward from a plain shaft end to a dark lower tip with a short left return and small opposite corner, read as one head. No decoration or terminal punctuation is supplied.

The first e has a small loop and long low return; the final t has a tall curved stem and dark diagonal crossing stroke. The intervening s is compressed into the low run and cannot be securely separated, so it remains a local doubt. No punctuation is added.

Complete central diagram; neighboring prose across the upper edge is excluded. The upper row has two pi symbols, each with a top bar and two legs, and short downward arrows. Between them are a long lower horizontal and a much shorter upper horizontal overlapping a prose descender; equality is favored but remains doubtful because the stroke roles and unequal lengths are not fully separable. The middle-left E has a detached faint upper-right curl that may belong to its first lobe or constitute a separate cap; bare/capped E is retained locally. All E bodies are curved and rendered calligraphic; U entries remain open. The U subscripts have a further S at left and branched K at right. Bottom nodes are E_S and E_K. The middle horizontal has one clear left head and a plain right tail. Both middle-to-bottom vertical connectors point down. The lower horizontal points left and bears surj below without a secure final stop; its shaft is retraced and two upper return strokes appear near the left tip. One head is favored but two remain possible. The dashed diagonal goes from lower-right to middle-left and bears varphi, with an upper loop and descending stem. At its upper-left end are two nearly parallel short upper returns and one lower return, favoring two heads while leaving one possible. Local unsure wrappers on arrow commands record these head-count doubts rather than adding arrows. The source label has a faint open numeral form, a short raised tick, and closing parenthesis: 4-prime is favored, with 5 unresolved. It is not regularized from sequence.

Both current K indices are dark and branched, with upper diagonal and lower arm. Each overlaps a paler rounded/curving index tentatively read S. The left old form begins with a small upper curl beneath U; the right has a narrow loop and lower return under K. Superseded letters remain doubtful, and replacement is represented with deleted/inserted markup. No separate horizontal cancellation is claimed beyond the overwriting. The intervening sur has three low joined bodies. E has two curved lobes; U has an open entry. A clipped lower neighboring stroke is excluded.

Revision scope is substantially uncertain. The leftmost short group has an a-like body, separate upper oblique, low run, and crossed terminal strokes: aux is favored, with à un alternative. The long cancellation begins to its right and runs through the baseline phrase to de at far right. The first crossed group is tentatively les mêmes; its boundaries are obscured by the strike and the descender of raised writing. A separate lower line runs approximately from source x600,y2071 to x739,y2056 under part of this group. Exact lexical underline extent remains uncertain, so the unsure wrapper includes the underline markup. Sections and final de remain readable beneath the strike. The comma after sections has a dark lower tail, while its top meets the strike; canceled/live status is unsettled. Above are two raised words. The first has an initial descending stroke, tall interior loop/stem, upper point, low joined returns, and high angular ending; précisément/plusieurs remain tentative. The second has a small initial curve, low joined bodies, tall crossed stroke, upper point, and long low ending; certaines/sections remain unresolved. This raised phrase is represented as an insertion over the crossed baseline without a finer chronology or syntactic completion. Revision state of the leftmost group remains uncertain; the TSV leaves it outside the long-strike deletion. Clipped upper-edge material belongs to the previous line and is excluded.

Complete l'hom. The l has a tall loop followed by a separate dark apostrophe. The h has a tall plain stem and low shoulder; o/m is compressed and flat with a short terminal hook. No separate stop is visible. The abbreviation is unexpanded.

The raised live triviaux has crossed t, low r/i with detached dot, v, second dotted i, a small a oval, low u, and faint crossed terminal strokes read x. Below, a short word is crossed by a heavy line and tentatively read nuls: low repeated cups and an interior rising stroke survive, but boundaries remain doubtful. A small isolated dot above the lower group cannot be securely assigned to a canceled letter. At right, a separate lower descending mark follows the strike endpoint; it may be comma or part of the canceled ending. It is represented as a doubtful comma, with live/canceled status unresolved. Replacement is physically raised; no sequence beyond visible cancellation and insertion is assigned.
Separate bottom-left foliation 63. The 6 has a long rising entry and closed lower loop; 3 has two curved right lobes and lower leftward foot. It uses margin markup.
